reason: The hypothesis relies on SCCPs for radiation tolerance, but the cited evidence (E1–E3) only demonstrates SCCPs for mechanical properties in a different alloy system (W-Ni-Fe-Ta) and does not address irradiation effects. E4 describes the baseline WxTaTiVCr alloy but provides no data on irradiation or SCCPs. Thus, the key premises about SCCP formation in the proposed alloy and their radiation-tolerance benefits are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates (SCCPs) can be formed in a W-based refractory HEA by a thermal annealing protocol (850–1100 °C, 1–2 h, rapid quench).
SCCPs serve as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced defects (e.g., He bubbles) and relieve stress concentrations.
SCCPs reduce irradiation-induced hardening and improve microstructural stability under He ion irradiation at ~1023 K.
The baseline WxTaTiVCr alloy without SCCPs exhibits more pronounced irradiation damage and higher hardening.
